 5.1 Subject access and data-protection complaint timeframes

  delay and ordinarily within one calendar month from the applicable starting point. A necessary
  complexity/number-of-requests extension requires notice and reasons within the initial period.
  Identification, a lawful fee or reasonably required clarification may affect the calculation only where
  the applicable conditions are met. If DWP received the SAR on 17 July, without an applicable timing
  adjustment, the ordinary response date was 17 August, 53 calendar days before this submission.
  Please provide the actual calculation, notices and delivery evidence; internal routing alone does not
  establish a valid adjustment. [1] See section 9.1.



  Revised legal basis. DPA 2018 section 164A(3)–(5) requires acknowledgement within the 30-day
  period beginning when the complaint is received, appropriate steps to respond without undue delay,
  progress information and notification of the outcome without undue delay. The relevant duties apply
  to complaints received on or after 19 June 2026. If DWP received my data-protection complaint on 31
  August, 39 calendar days had elapsed by 9 October and the 30-day acknowledgement period had
  expired. Please provide the receipt and acknowledgement records, enquiries, updates and outcome,
  or explain what remains outstanding and when it will be completed. Keep this separate from the SAR
  and service-complaint clocks. [2] See section 9.1.

 complaint is received, appropriate enquiries and progress information, and an outcome without
 undue delay: subsections (2)–(5). On receipt on 31 August, 39 calendar days had elapsed by 9
 October, beyond the acknowledgement period; actual receipt and steps taken remain to be
 established. Regulations 3(a) and 7 of the commencement instrument apply the
 acknowledgement/response duties to complaints received on or after 19 June 2026. Please identify
